historical_transitions.summary: WildcatArchController deployed at block 18686645 (2023-11-30) by EOA 0xb4B9f935bf0189c2FF46165F04b0D517e9553FBc: the non-proxy singleton registry recording borrowers, hooks factories and market templates for Wildcat's undercollateralised credit markets. The deployment receipt emits OwnershipTransferred(address(0) -> 0xb4B9...3FBc); runtime code 8724 bytes, verified source on Blockscout.

First ownership rotation eight days after deployment: the ArchController emits OwnershipTransferred(0xb4B9...3FBc -> 0x0c2914fd10086443A8800e2bB5258d4C463a88A0) at block 18743312, moving control from the deployer EOA to a 2-of-3 Safe (threshold/owners confirmed via getThreshold/getOwners on 0x0c29...88A0).

Second rotation at block 21788112 (2025-02-06 14:38 UTC), minutes before the V2 periphery launch: the 2-of-3 Safe executes transferOwnership and the ArchController emits OwnershipTransferred(0x0c29...88A0 -> 0x240334405021F4242d57a3785df39Edc23E1B607).

Wildcat V2 mainnet expansion: HooksFactory 0xDd7dd3b5076Cf89440d05585FF56d246386207Be deployed at block 21788182 (WildcatMarket initCodeStorage 0xAc3216FA28F81B8FaE150fB5626ca79C7a570DAf same day at 21788178, tx 0x2ac9bce6eeabd55459dcc70d4474d3b5cce2dd08cd340a6bd095143fb3727f41). V2 adds hook-templated market behaviour while reusing the immutable V1 ArchController as registry; no replacement controller was deployed.

Final ownership handover at block 21788248 (2025-02-06 15:05 UTC), completing the EOA-to-Safe migration 27 minutes after it began: the ArchController emits OwnershipTransferred(0x2403...B607 -> 0xC15bE5214978d1fc509ECdd4f9D5BC067C94D9Ae). owner() has remained that 3-of-5 Safe ever since (eth_call owner() at latest block).

Immutability checkpoint at block 26451708 (2026-11-19 21:05 UTC): the 3-of-5 Safe 0xC15b...D9Ae executes addBorrower through the same V1 registry (ArchController BorrowerAdded log in this receipt). Runtime bytecode is byte-identical across the whole window: sha256 prefix 4988e6580cf924ab at blocks 18686645, 26450616 (Pacta pin) and 26451708, 8724 bytes each; no proxy upgrade, selfdestruct or redeploy across 2023-2026.

evidence_sources.claim_summary: Initial publication of whitepaper_v2.0.pdf ('Create whitepaper_v2.0.pdf', first commit in the file's history): the V2 specification shipped publicly 163 days before the V2 mainnet deployment at block 21788182.
GITBOOK-140 'Duplicating Terms of Use page to adjust V2 app appropriateness': V2 web-documentation edits landed three weeks before the 2025-02-06 mainnet deployment.

Pre-deploy snapshot of docs.wildcat.finance already shows a 'V1 -> V2 Changelog' nav entry and notes the docs 'recently underwent substantial changes to incorporate Wildcat V2 details': web documentation tracked V2 before mainnet launch.

Post-deploy refresh ('Update whitepaper_v2.0.pdf') of the already-public V2 whitepaper two days after mainnet launch: a modification of the existing v2.0 PDF (first committed 2024-08-27), not its initial publication.

The v2-protocol README (last touched 2024-08-29, before V2 launch) still labels both the whitepaper and the V1 GitBook '[Out Of Date For V2]': a stale signpost that survives 651 days after V2 went live, even though the whitepaper itself is the current v2.0 spec.

gap_windows.summary: Stale-pointer documentation-hygiene gap: since V2 launch the v2-protocol README has directed auditors to the whitepaper and V1 GitBook as '[Out Of Date For V2]' without revision, 651 days (2025-02-06 -> 2026-11-19) and counting. The whitepaper itself was never part of a spec gap: v2.0 was first published 2024-08-27, 163 days before deployment, and refreshed two days after launch (2025-02-08).

executive_risk_memo: Wildcat is an undercollateralised credit protocol whose control plane is the WildcatArchController, a non-proxy singleton registry deployed 2023-11-30 at block 18686645 and byte-identical at the 2026-11-19 pinned block (sha256 prefix 4988e6580cf924ab at blocks 18686645, 26450616 and 26451708): the registry cannot be upgraded in place, the strongest possible posture for a core contract. Ownership is the mutable surface, and it migrated deliberately: the deployer EOA 0xb4B9...3FBc rotated to a 2-of-3 Safe (0x0c29...88A0) eight days after deployment, then through EOA 0x2403...B607 to the current 3-of-5 Safe 0xC15b...D9Ae in a 27-minute sequence straddling the 2025-02-06 V2 periphery launch, every step an on-chain OwnershipTransferred receipt. Governance capture of that Safe is the primary residual risk because it alone registers borrowers, hooks factories and market templates. The V2 expansion shifted safety invariants from core code into borrower-selected hook configuration, so lender protection now depends on per-market hook choices rather than protocol-wide enforcement. Engineering bandwidth is thin: the v2-protocol repository recorded 6 commits in the trailing 12 months from 3 human authors (d1ll0n, laurenceday, 0xMcsweeja), with contract-surface work concentrated in two engineers (bus factor 2). Documentation tracked the V2 launch well - the v2.0 whitepaper was first published 163 days before deployment and refreshed two days after - yet the repository README still signposts superseded V1 material 651 days later, an unrepaired hygiene gap. DefiLlama non-borrowed TVL is volatile (roughly $2.7M-$16.7M over the trailing 60 days) and sits near the Wave 3 floor at submission time. Overall: immutable core, small team, mutable periphery; residual risk is governance capture and hook misconfiguration, not code upgradeability.
